title: Services also covered pre-fills the covered services' lines
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in, on the build under test, as an Owner/Admin or as a user with "Settings Service" enabled.
  2. In the left sidebar under Settings, open the "Maintenance" entry beneath "Inspection Templates" (if the build shows "Maintenance schedules" instead, use that entry and record the label). Schedules are shared by the whole organization, whichever location is chosen in the header.
  3. A schedule with routine services and one compliance service. Seed it:
  4. ↳ New schedule; Add service "PM-A" (Every 3 months, 3 canned lines) and "PM-B" (Every 6 months, 2 canned lines); save each.
  5. ↳ Add service "CVIP": turn on "Is this a compliance inspection?", Type "CVIP", Term 12 months; save it.
custom_steps:
1. Click Add service, name it "PM-C", go to the "Services also covered" step and read its guidance line and the list offered.
  2. Leave the covered step empty on a second new service "PM-X" whose canned line is the same as one of PM-A's, and save it; check whether anything was ticked for you.
  3. Pick PM-A and PM-B, go to the canned-lines step and read the lines and their markers; remove one line marked "from PM-A".
  4. Save PM-C, then open PM-A and PM-B again.
  5. Start a fresh schedule, click Add service for its first service, and check whether the covered step shows; then open the CVIP service and check the same.
  6. Edit PM-A, open its covered step and look for PM-C in the list.
  7. Add service "PM-D", pick only PM-C at the covered step, and look at whether PM-A and PM-B are ticked.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • The step shows one line of guidance to build the smallest service first, and lists only PM-A and PM-B (the existing routine services); CVIP is not offered.
  • PM-X saves with nothing covered: covering is never filled in from shared lines or interval length; only what the shop picks is covered.
  • PM-A's 3 lines and PM-B's 2 lines arrive pre-filled and editable, each marked "from PM-A" or "from PM-B".
  • Removing a "from PM-A" line in PM-C leaves PM-A's own lines unchanged; PM-C's line count reads "4 lines · 4 covered" (5 covered lines − 1 removed = 4).
  • On a first service and on a compliance service the covered step does not show, and the steps after it move up by one.
  • PM-C is not offered when editing PM-A, because PM-C already covers PM-A.
  • Picking PM-C does not also pick PM-A or PM-B; each covered service has to be named.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-3780, story SV-10559 (S2, Add a routine service to a schedule), Chunk 1 MR (Confluence 886931488) as edited 5 October 2026, S2 (Services also covered; S2-R16 to S2-R19, S2-N8, S2-N9, S2-E6); Design board "Chunk 1.dc.html" (MR V2 Claude Design project, version of 6 October 2026), artboards R4 / R7 (Services also covered); read 6 Oct 2026. Source-verified 6 October 2026; not yet build-verified.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S2-R16: “A service can name the other services on its schedule that it also covers, in a step before canned lines: a multi-select of the schedule's other services”
  • S2-R19: “The step carries one line of guidance: build the smallest service first. A service can only name services that already exist on the schedule”
  • S2-E6: “A service may cover nothing, and most will. Covering is never inferred from shared canned lines or from interval length; a shop states it”
  • S2-R17: “The covered services' canned lines arrive in the canned lines step pre-filled and editable, each marked with the service it came from, for example from PM-A”
  • S2-R17: “Changing or removing them here changes this service only, never the one they came from”
  • S2-R18: “On the first service, and on every compliance service, the step is not shown and the steps after it move up by one”
  • S2-N9: “A service cannot cover a service that already covers it, directly or through another; the list does not offer it”
  • S2-N9: “Covering is not inherited: a service names every service it covers. In the canned-lines count, N covered counts the lines that came from covered services”
  • S2-N8: “A compliance service is never offered in the picker and cannot name services of its own. It covers nothing and is covered by nothing”
  • Design board, artboard R4: “Build the smallest service first. PM-C covers PM-A and PM-B, so their lines arrive in the next step.”
